author: mvafin
title: Merge-queue run cancelled after being superseded by a newer run on the same ref
signature: context canceled the operation was canceled|Infrastructure

failed_jobs.name: iGPU RoPE Tests / GPU_RoPE
failed_jobs.symptom: Download OpenVINO artifacts (package) step aborted mid-download with 'context canceled' / 'The operation was canceled.'

root_cause: The run's overall conclusion was 'cancelled' (not 'failure'). Only one job ('iGPU RoPE Tests / GPU_RoPE') actually shows a cancelled conclusion, and its logs show a generic 'context canceled' / 'The operation was canceled.' error mid-way through an artifact download step -- there is no application-level error. All other 38 jobs in the run were 'success' or 'skipped'. The ubuntu_22.yml workflow (and its sibling per-OS workflows) define concurrency.group as `${{ github.ref }}-ubuntu-22` with cancel-in-progress: true (lines 27-30). Merge-queue runs share the same head_branch (gh-readonly-queue/master/pr-38168-<sha>) across attempts/re-queues of the same PR, so github.ref is identical across consecutive runs for this PR. Listing workflow runs on that same head_branch shows two later runs (35653415300 and the in-progress 35653600791) created shortly after this run started, both on the identical concurrency group key. GitHub Actions' cancel-in-progress concurrency control therefore cancelled this older, still-running run 35643124789 in favor of the newer one, which is the expected/intended behavior of the cancel-in-progress concurrency guard rather than a code, dependency, or test defect.
reproduction_steps: N/A - not reproducible as a code/test failure. To confirm the same behavior: trigger two merge-queue attempts for the same PR in quick succession and observe that the earlier run's jobs are cancelled once the newer run starts, because both share the concurrency group `${{ github.ref }}-ubuntu-22` with cancel-in-progress: true.
recommended_actions: No code fix needed for this PR; the run was intentionally superseded by concurrency control, not an application failure.

If this canceled-and-superseded pattern recurs, verify the merge-queue is not repeatedly re-queuing the same PR/commit (e.g., due to flaky prerequisite checks) which would waste CI capacity on runs that are cancelled before completing.
Rely on the newer, still-in-progress run (35653415300 / 35653600791) for the actual pass/fail signal for this PR revision.
prevention_strategies: This is expected GitHub Actions concurrency-group behavior (cancel-in-progress: true) and does not need prevention, but repeated re-queues of the same PR causing repeated cancellations may indicate an upstream flakiness/re-add loop worth monitoring via the pattern database's occurrence count.
historical_context: No prior CI Doctor MQ investigation recorded this exact 'superseded-by-newer-run cancellation' signature; other stored Infrastructure patterns involve runner shutdown signals or jobs cancelled before runner assignment, which are distinct failure modes from a cancel-in-progress concurrency-group supersession.
